items.title: Leonardo’s UK Loss Shows the Cost of Renting Hotels
items.summary: Leonardo's UK hotels are making money from guests, but not enough to cover the rent. With costs rising and more rooms coming onto the market, the lease-heavy model that let hotel groups expand fast in the UK is starting to look like a liability.

items.title: Norse Atlantic Collapses as Norwegian Arm Files for Bankruptcy
items.summary: Norse’s efforts to diversify beyond low-cost, long-haul flying ultimately proved insufficient to keep its planes in the air. The focus now shifts to what, if anything, can be salvaged from the business.

items.title: Hotelbeds’ $112 Million Bet as Its Core Business Comes Under Pressure
items.summary: Hotelbeds is accepting a lower take rate to gain market share, while investing in new sources of revenue.

items.title: Why Global Hotel Alliance Is Turning to Saudi Arabia Despite Riyadh’s Slump
items.summary: GHA is coming through a hard year in the UAE as one of the country's largest loyalty players. Its CEO doesn't want to grow much more there. He's betting on Saudi Arabia instead, even as Riyadh's hotels struggle.

items.title: Agoda’s COO on AI Booking: ‘Nobody Knows’ the Business Model Yet
items.summary: Agoda wants to win AI agents' business the way it wins travelers': on price, speed and reliability. What it can't say yet is what those agents will eventually cost it, and that answer will matter more to its margins than any integration.

items.title: Dubai Gets Some Airlines Back as Riyadh Waits on Houthis
items.summary: Dubai's airline return hinges on a regulator's deadline. Riyadh's depends on weeks without strikes, and until then its hotels lose the regional traffic that fills them midweek.

items.title: Travelodge’s New CEO Inherits Safety Reckoning, Rising Costs and Looming Debt
items.summary: Travelodge has a new chief executive, 38 safety recommendations to implement, and debt to refinance. Peter Krueger starts Tuesday.

items.title: In Praise of Kiwi.com
items.summary: Kiwi pioneered a better way to find flights, but the economics of selling and servicing them proved harder.
